passages.text: “Go down and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, O Daughter of Chaldea! For you will no longer be called tender or delicate.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to Babylon.
Babylon is called the Virgin Daughter of Babylon.
Babylon is also called the Daughter of Chaldea.
The Lord commands Babylon to go down.
The Lord tells Babylon to sit in the dust.
The Lord tells Babylon to sit on the ground.
Babylon will not have a throne.
Babylon will lose its royal seat.
People will not call Babylon tender anymore.
People will not call Babylon delicate anymore.
passages.original: רְדִ֣י׀ וּשְׁבִ֣י עַל־ עָפָ֗ר בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־ בָּבֶ֔ל שְׁבִי־ לָאָ֥רֶץ אֵין־ כִּסֵּ֖א בַּת־ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י לֹ֤א תוֹסִ֙יפִי֙ יִקְרְאוּ־ לָ֔ךְ רַכָּ֖ה וַעֲנֻגָּֽה׃

passages.text: Take millstones and grind flour; remove your veil; strip off your skirt, bare your thigh, and wade through the streams.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the Daughter of Babylon.
He commands her to take millstones.
He tells her to grind flour.
He tells her to remove her veil.
He tells her to strip off her skirt.
He tells her to bare her thigh.
He tells her to wade through the streams.
passages.original: קְחִ֥י רֵחַ֖יִם וְטַ֣חֲנִי קָ֑מַח גַּלִּ֨י צַמָּתֵ֧ךְ חֶשְׂפִּי־ שֹׁ֛בֶל גַּלִּי־ שׁ֖וֹק עִבְרִ֥י נְהָרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed. I will take vengeance; I will spare no one.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
God says, “People will uncover your nakedness.
People will see your shame.
I will take vengeance on you.
I will not spare anyone.”
passages.original: תִּגָּל֙ עֶרְוָתֵ֔ךְ גַּ֥ם תֵּרָאֶ֖ה חֶרְפָּתֵ֑ךְ נָקָ֣ם אֶקָּ֔ח וְלֹ֥א אֶפְגַּ֖ע אָדָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Our Redeemer—the LORD of Hosts is His name— is the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon: The LORD of Hosts is our Redeemer.\r\nHis name is the LORD of Hosts.\r\nHe is the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of Chaldea. For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to the Daughter of Chaldea.
You are the people of Babylon.
You lived in pride and power.
Now sit in silence.
Go into darkness.
You will not be called the queen of kingdoms anymore.
passages.original: שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי בַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ בַּת־ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י לֹ֤א תוֹסִ֙יפִי֙ יִקְרְאוּ־ לָ֔ךְ גְּבֶ֖רֶת מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I was angry with My people; I profaned My heritage, and I placed them under your control. You showed them no mercy; even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the Holy One of Israel.
He is our Redeemer.
He became angry with His people.
He treated His own people as common.
He gave His people into your power.
You showed them no mercy.
You made their suffering very hard.
You made the burden especially heavy for the elderly.
passages.original: קָצַ֣פְתִּי עַל־ עַמִּ֗י חִלַּ֙לְתִּי֙ נַחֲלָתִ֔י וָאֶתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיָדֵ֑ךְ לֹא־ שַׂ֤מְתְּ לָהֶם֙ רַחֲמִ֔ים עַל־ זָקֵ֕ן הִכְבַּ֥דְתְּ עֻלֵּ֖ךְ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: You said, ‘I will be queen forever.’ You did not take these things to heart or consider their outcome.
passages.sermon:
The Daughter of Chaldea was proud.
She said, “I will be queen forever.”
She did not think about what would happen in the end.
She did not take these warnings seriously.
She did not remember what her actions would bring.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמְרִ֔י לְעוֹלָ֖ם אֶהְיֶ֣ה גְבָ֑רֶת עַ֣ד לֹא־ שַׂ֥מְתְּ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ עַל־ לִבֵּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א זָכַ֖רְתְּ אַחֲרִיתָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: So now hear this, O lover of luxury who sits securely, who says to herself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me. I will never be a widow or know the loss of children.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
Babylon loves luxury.
Babylon sits in safety.
Babylon feels secure.
Babylon says in her heart, “I am important.”
Babylon says, “No one else matters but me.”
Babylon says, “I will never become a widow.”
Babylon says, “I will never lose my children.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי־ זֹ֤את עֲדִינָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָ֔בָהּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד לֹ֤א אֵשֵׁב֙ אַלְמָנָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אֵדַ֖ע שְׁכֽוֹל׃

passages.text: These two things will overtake you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children, and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
Babylon is proud and trusts in her own power.
Babylon believes she is secure and above all others.
Two disasters will come to Babylon.
These disasters are loss of children and widowhood.
Both disasters will strike suddenly.
They will happen in a single day.
These troubles will come in full measure.
Babylon uses many sorceries and powerful spells.
Her sorceries and spells will not protect her.
Disaster will come despite all her magic.
passages.original: וְתָבֹאנָה֩ לָּ֨ךְ שְׁתֵּי־ אֵ֥לֶּה רֶ֛גַע בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד שְׁכ֣וֹל וְאַלְמֹ֑ן כְּתֻמָּם֙ בָּ֣אוּ עָלַ֔יִךְ בְּרֹ֣ב כְּשָׁפַ֔יִךְ בְּעָצְמַ֥ת חֲבָרַ֖יִךְ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: You were secure in your wickedness; you said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray; you told yourself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.’
passages.sermon:
You trusted in your wickedness.
You felt safe because of your evil deeds.
You said, “No one sees me.”
You believed you could hide your actions.
Your wisdom misled you.
Your knowledge led you astray.
You thought you were wise.
You said in your heart, “I am the only one.”
You said, “There is no one besides me.”
passages.original: וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְרָעָתֵ֗ךְ אָמַרְתְּ֙ אֵ֣ין רֹאָ֔נִי חָכְמָתֵ֥ךְ וְדַעְתֵּ֖ךְ הִ֣יא שׁוֹבְבָ֑תֶךְ וַתֹּאמְרִ֣י בְלִבֵּ֔ךְ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֥י עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: But disaster will come upon you; you will not know how to charm it away. A calamity will befall you that you will be unable to ward off. Devastation will happen to you suddenly and unexpectedly.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
Babylon is proud and trusts in sorcery.
Disaster will come upon you.
You will not know how to stop it.
A calamity will fall on you.
You will not be able to prevent it.
Devastation will strike you suddenly.
You will not expect it.
passages.original: וּבָ֧א עָלַ֣יִךְ רָעָ֗ה לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ שַׁחְרָ֔הּ וְתִפֹּ֤ל עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ הֹוָ֔ה לֹ֥א תוּכְלִ֖י כַּפְּרָ֑הּ וְתָבֹ֨א עָלַ֧יִךְ פִּתְאֹ֛ם שׁוֹאָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵדָֽעִי׃

passages.text: So take your stand with your spells and with your many sorceries, with which you have wearied yourself from your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
Babylon trusted in sorcery and magic since youth.
Babylon worked hard at spells and sorceries for many years.
God says, “Stand now with your companions.
Use your many spells and sorceries.
You have grown tired from these practices since you were young.
Perhaps you will be able to help yourself.
Perhaps you will cause fear in others.”
passages.original: עִמְדִי־ נָ֤א בַחֲבָרַ֙יִךְ֙ וּבְרֹ֣ב כְּשָׁפַ֔יִךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגַ֖עַתְּ מִנְּעוּרָ֑יִךְ אוּלַ֛י תּוּכְלִ֥י הוֹעִ֖יל אוּלַ֥י תַּעֲרֽוֹצִי׃

passages.text: You are wearied by your many counselors; let them come forward now and save you— your astrologers who observe the stars, who monthly predict your fate.
passages.sermon:
You have many counselors.
They give you advice.
You are tired from listening to them.
Let your counselors come forward now.
Let them try to save you.
You have astrologers.
They look at the stars.
They tell you what will happen each month.
They predict your future.
Let them save you from what is coming.
passages.original: נִלְאֵ֖ית בְּרֹ֣ב עֲצָתָ֑יִךְ יַעַמְדוּ־ נָ֨א וְיוֹשִׁיעֻ֜ךְ הָבְרוּ שָׁמַ֗יִם הַֽחֹזִים֙ בַּכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים מֽוֹדִיעִם֙ לֶחֳדָשִׁ֔ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖אוּ עָלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up. They cannot deliver themselves from the power of the flame. There will be no coals to warm them or fire to sit beside.
passages.sermon:
These people trust in sorcery and false counsel.
They are weak and helpless.
They are like dry stubble.
Fire will burn them up quickly.
They cannot save themselves from the flames.
The fire will destroy them completely.
No coals will remain for warmth.
No fire will be left to sit beside.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה הָי֤וּ כְקַשׁ֙ אֵ֣שׁ שְׂרָפָ֔תַם לֹֽא־ יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־ נַפְשָׁ֖ם מִיַּ֣ד לֶֽהָבָ֑ה אֵין־ גַּחֶ֣לֶת לַחְמָ֔ם א֖וּר לָשֶׁ֥בֶת נֶגְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This is what they are to you— those with whom you have labored and traded from youth— each one strays in his own direction; not one of them can save you.
passages.sermon:
These people have been with you since you were young.
You worked hard with them.
You traded with them.
Each one of them goes his own way.
None of them can save you.
passages.original: כֵּ֥ן הָיוּ־ לָ֖ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָגָ֑עַתְּ סֹחֲרַ֣יִךְ מִנְּעוּרַ֗יִךְ אִ֤ישׁ לְעֶבְרוֹ֙ תָּע֔וּ אֵ֖ין מוֹשִׁיעֵֽךְ׃ס
